entry.title: Issues with the New SAP Certification Exam Format
entry.content:

entry.title: SAP Cloud Integration (Subaccount B)→ SQM (Subaccount A) Connectivity & Authentication
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

We are currently evaluating a change in our integration architecture and would appreciate guidance from anyone with experience integrating SAP Cloud Integration with SAP Ariba Supplier Quotation Management (SQM).. Below is the official help.sap documentation for SQM ..

SAP Ariba Supplier Quotation Management (Legacy Version) | SAP Help Portal | SAP Help Portal

Landscape

Global Account

  • Single SAP BTP Global Account

Subaccount A

  • SAP Event Mesh
  • SAP Ariba Supplier Quotation Management (SQM)

Subaccount B

  • SAP Integration Suite (Cloud Integration)

Current Flow (Working)

SAP RISE
↓
SAP Event Mesh (Subaccount A)
↓
SAP Ariba Supplier Quotation Management (SQM)

Target Flow

SAP RISE
↓
SAP Event Mesh (Subaccount A)
↓
SAP Cloud Integration (Subaccount B)
↓
SAP Ariba Supplier Quotation Management (SQM)

What We Have Confirmed

  • Cloud Integration can connect to SAP Event Mesh in another subaccount using AMQP and Event Mesh service key credentials.
  • Both subaccounts belong to the same BTP Global Account.
  • Event Mesh is a standalone SAP Event Mesh service and not the Event Mesh capability embedded in Integration Suite.

Open Questions

  1. Has anyone implemented a scenario where Cloud Integration consumes messages from Event Mesh and subsequently sends them to SAP Ariba Supplier Quotation Management (SQM)?

  2. What is the officially supported inbound integration approach for SQM?

    • REST API?
    • OData API?
    • Communication Arrangement?
    • Ariba API Gateway?

  3. How should Cloud Integration authenticate against SQM?

    • OAuth2 Client Credentials?
    • Communication User?
    • Ariba API Key?
    • Other supported mechanism?

  4. Is there any official documentation describing:

    • Supported inbound APIs for SQM
    • Endpoint URLs
    • Authentication requirements
    • OAuth client onboarding

  5. Since SQM is available as a SaaS subscription (application plan) and not as a service instance, should a separate XSUAA instance be created for system-to-system communication, or does SQM require a different authentication model?

Challenge

We are currently unable to locate the API documentation and supported inbound endpoints for SQM. The SAP Help Portal documentation appears to focus mainly on the application and business processes, but we have not yet found a clear guide for Cloud Integration → SQM system-to-system integrations. Any guidance, documentation references, or implementation experiences would be greatly appreciated. Thank you in advance.

Best regards, Ramu..

entry.title: Integration Cell artifact stuck in Starting/Deploying and endpoint never becomes available-btp trial
entry.content:
Hi SAP Community,
 
I am encountering an issue with API Management artifacts deployed to the Integration Cell runtime in a newly created SAP BTP Trial subaccount.
 
Environment:
• SAP BTP Trial (US10)
• Integration Suite trial subscription
• Integration Cell status: Active
• Capabilities enabled: Cloud Integration, API Management, Developer Hub, API Composition
 
Issue:
I created an API artifact from an OpenAPI 3.0 specification containing a single GET operation and deployed it to the Integration Cell runtime.
 
After deployment:
• The artifact remains in "Starting" state indefinitely.
• The Endpoints tab shows "There are no endpoints configured."
• In some cases, the artifact eventually moves to "Error" with the message "The API is not operational."
• No additional error details are available in the monitoring views.
 
Configuration verified:
• Valid API Base Path configured.
• Resources are correctly generated from the OpenAPI specification.
• Backend target endpoint is configured.
• Runtime Profile is Integration Cell.
• Virtual host is assigned and the API URL is generated correctly in the artifact overview.
 
Additional observations:
• Accessing the Integration Cell virtual host returns HTTP 503 (server: istio-envoy).
• The issue persists after undeploying, deleting, and recreating the API artifact.
• This is a completely fresh trial subaccount and the first artifact being deployed.
 
Has anyone experienced a similar issue where API artifacts deployed to Integration Cell never become operational and endpoints are not published? Is there any way to verify that the Integration Cell workload behind the virtual host has been provisioned correctly?
 
Any guidance would be greatly appreciated.
 
Thank you!

entry.title: Different average exchange rates depending on when a consolidation unit enters the cons. group
entry.content:
Hello All,

 

Good day!

 

We are using S/4 Hana Private Version 2023 FPS02. 

 

A requirement has arisen at one of our clients regarding the translation of foreign currency financial statements in SAP Group Reporting.

 

The business requirement is to apply a different average exchange rate depending on when a consolidation unit enters the consolidation group.

 

For example, the standard AVG (average exchange rate) is calculated as the accumulated average exchange rate from the beginning of the year up to the current conversion period. This rate is currently used to translate the consolidation units that are already part of the group consolidation.

 

However, when a new consolidation unit enters the consolidation group during the year, the requirement is to apply a different average exchange rate to this newly consolidated unit, rather than using the same AVG rate that is applied to the units that have already been part of the consolidation group.

 

In other words, we would need to have more than one average exchange rate for the same currency pair, depending on the date/period in which the consolidation unit enters the consolidation group:

 

Existing consolidation units: use the standard accumulated AVG rate up to the current conversion period.

Newly consolidated units: use a different AVG rate, based on the specific date/period in which the unit enters the consolidation group.

For example, if a consolidation unit enters the group in period 06/2026, we would need to use a different average exchange rate for this unit from period 06 onwards, while the other consolidation units would continue using the standard accumulated AVG rate.

 

Is this requirement technically feasible in SAP Group Reporting?

 

Is there any standard functionality or configuration that allows different AVG exchange rates to be applied to different consolidation units within the same consolidation group, depending on when they enter the consolidation scope?

 

Has anyone encountered a similar business requirement or implemented a solution for this scenario in Group Reporting?

 

Any advice or recommendations regarding the standard configuration or possible workarounds would be greatly appreciated.

 

Thanks in advance!

entry.title: Not able to Connect to SAP MCP Server with IBM BOB or Github Co-Pilot on Visual Studio Code
entry.content:
Hello Experts and Mentors,

I have a requirement to connect to SAP MCP Servers to explore the SAP BTP Adminisration Task Scenarios and utilize the relevant use cases available.
So I initially started with the below code snippet.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "btp-administration": {
      "type": "streamable-http",
      "url": "https://sso.mcp.btp.cloud.sap/mcp",
      "alwaysAllow": [],
      "disabled": false
    }
  }
}

 However with the above code snippet the MCP Server was showing disconnected and the error message was
"Authentication Required The Server failed to connect. Check the logs for error details or try restarting the server"

After that I tried the below code snippet

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "btp-administration": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote",
        "https://sso.mcp.btp.cloud.sap/mcp"
      ],
      "disabled": false
    }
  }
}

After that the Error message was different.
MCP Error - 32000:Connection closed The Server Failed to connect. Check the logs for error details or try restarting the server.

After further researching what I understood is that the child process BOB tried to spawn exited immediately before any MCP handshake happened. That is related to Node Package Execute (npx) issue. npx is actually npx.cmd  and many clients fail to spawn .cmd files directly without going through shell.
Next Step which I tried is as below by running the command in cmd.
npx -y mcp-remote https://sso.mcp.btp.cloud.sap/mcp

This time the error message was 
Connection Error: Registration RejectedError: Dynamic Client Registration rejected  (HTTP 401) : Bad credentials

Reason was that mcp-remote was trying to self-register a new client instead of using SAP's pre-registered one.
Next Step tried was to pass the Client ID SAP Published via --static-oauth-client-info

This is the below command that was tried.
npx -y mcp-remote https://sso.mcp.btp.cloud.sap/mcp --static-oauth-client-info "{ \"client_id\": \"e789ba01-5612-47ee-bfe7-79e26411c1ca\" }"

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "btp-administration": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote",
        "https://sso.mcp.btp.cloud.sap/mcp",
        "--static-oauth-client-info",
        "{ \"client_id\": \"e789ba01-5612-47ee-bfe7-79e26411c1ca\" }"
      ],
      "disabled": false
    }
  }
}

The Error message encountered as below
OpenID provider cannot process the request because the configuration is incorrect. Please contact your system administrator.

 

 

I have also tried to the same attempt through Github Co-Pilot by passing the Client ID but Similar Error is coming there as well.
What I understand that Github-CoPilot on Visual Studio Code is affiliated and approved tool by SAP.

Did anyone already faced the similar issue? 

Can you please suggest?
Appreciate your suggestions.

==================
Thanks and Regards
Anurag Das
==================
